title: Atomic Consistency Preference Optimization for Long-Form Question Answering
abstract: arXiv:2505.09039v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) often produce factoid hallucinations - plausible yet incorrect answers. A common mitigation strategy is model alignment, which improves factual accuracy by training on curated (factual, non-factual) pairs. However, this approach often relies on a stronger model (e.g., GPT-4) or an external knowledge base to assess factual correctness that may not always be accessible. Addressing this, we propose Atomic Consistency Preference Optimization (ACPO), a self-supervised preference-tuning method that enhances factual accuracy without external supervision. ACPO leverages atomic consistency signals (i.e., the agreement of individual facts across multiple stochastic responses) to identify high- and low-quality data pairs for model alignment. Despite being fully self-supervised, ACPO outperforms the strong supervised alignment baseline by 1.95 points averaged across Phi-3 and Llama3 on the LongFact and BioGen dataset

translated_title: 面向长文本问答的原子一致性偏好优化
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）经常产生事实性幻觉——看似合理却错误的答案。一种常见的缓解策略是模型对齐，即通过在精选的（事实性、非事实性）数据对上训练来提高事实准确性。然而，这种方法通常依赖于更强大的模型（如GPT-4）或外部知识库来评估事实正确性，而这些资源并不总是可获取的。针对这一问题，我们提出了原子一致性偏好优化（ACPO），这是一种无需外部监督即可提升事实准确性的自监督偏好调优方法。ACPO利用原子一致性信号（即多个随机生成回复中各个原子事实的一致程度）来识别用于模型对齐的高质量和低质量数据对。尽管完全自监督，ACPO在LongFact和BioGen数据集上，于Phi-3和Llama3两个模型上的平均表现仍超过强监督对齐基线1.95个百分点。
tldr: 提出自监督偏好优化方法ACPO，利用多个随机回复间的原子事实一致性信号构建训练数据对，无需依赖外部强模型或知识库即可显著提升大语言模型长文本问答的事实准确性。
en_tdlr: ACPO is a fully self-supervised preference-tuning method that leverages atomic consistency signals across multiple stochastic responses to build training pairs, improving the factual accuracy of LLMs in long-form QA without requiring external supervision.
